harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s upload endpoint on TCP/8080. It accepts raw bodies through 65,536 bytes, returns 413 above the boundary without creating a receipt, stores each accepted body in a unique file, cleans interrupted uploads, returns 404 for other paths, and persists across reboot. The legacy receipt and installed OS/kernel were preserved. Both nodes passed sequential restart recovery checks.
actions_performed: Replaced the defective upload script with a Python 3 standard-library implementation using staged writes and atomic receipt publication.
Added and enabled a systemd service with failure restart behavior.
Opened TCP/8080 in node1’s runtime and permanent firewalld configuration.
Tested boundaries, byte identity, distinct receipts, unrelated paths, and interrupted requests from node2.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Accept raw request bodies through 65536 bytes and reject larger bodies with HTTP 413 before publishing a receipt
evidence.summary: Node2 received HTTP 200 for 1, 65535, and 65536 bytes and HTTP 413 for 65537 bytes. Node1 contains receipts only for accepted requests, including post-restart checks.

evidence.requirement: Store every accepted upload separately with identical bytes
evidence.summary: Distinct filenames were returned for accepted requests. Server-side sizes and SHA-256 digests match node2’s source payloads exactly.

evidence.requirement: Interrupted requests leave no completed receipt
evidence.summary: A request declaring 65536 bytes but sending only 1024 returned HTTP 400; receipt count remained unchanged and staging contained zero files.
POST /not-upload and GET /anything both returned HTTP 404.
received/prior.bin remains 28 bytes with SHA-256 ac9690aa0a0fe733a2702464777a0148b5a189d0a2f6eef1993268ebc70665fe and its original inode and modification time.
The enabled systemd service is active on 0.0.0.0:8080, and firewalld permits TCP/8080 in runtime and permanent configurations.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on CentOS Stream release 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 after the repair and restarts.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 4cee4ea8-4b8e-4c2f-af1a-3a82b9ec41f4; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID is 8f67c02d-f142-46aa-a122-542383af6eb3. Service, firewall, receipts, and 65536/65537 boundary behavior recovered.

Healthy client baseline used boot ID a70d7f83-6867-4c91-851d-7a1228689bb3; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID is 23b7436d-3a76-4806-85c9-d1c4a0da160b. Client data, routing, and endpoint boundary behavior recovered.
